$description: The Inspector's Style tab: the Target Line's host, one filter, then the CSS property accordion — every row saying where its value came from (§6.2), every section heading tallying what is set inside it. Nothing here knows what CSS is. `panels/style-panel.ts` resolves the compound coordinate (selection, breakpoint, scheme layer, nested selector), reads css-meta, decides which of seven controls a property gets, works out its provenance and what a commit writes; this document draws the answer and decides nothing. That split is what lets the tab stop going through `panels/panel-scheduler.ts`: the focus guard existed because a lit repaint of the whole panel could take the field a reader was typing into, and a document is one runtime effect per bound property with an equal write skipped.

style.$description: What `.style-sidebar`, `.style-filter-bar`, `.style-row`, `.style-row-label`, `.style-row--child`, `.style-row--warning`, `.style-shorthand-header`, `.style-section-body--grid`, `.kv-row`, `.kv-key`, `.kv-val`, `.input-group`, `.style-input-number-unit`, `.button-group-combo`, `.provenance-chip*`, `.set-dot` and `.provenance-dots` said across `styles/inspector.css` and `styles/overlays.css`, keyed on `part` and re-pointed at the kit's token layer. The rules those parts replace are DEAD in the stylesheets now rather than shared: `ui/field-row.ts` drew the same row for the Signals panel and the expression editor, and it is gone with them, so `.style-row*`, `.provenance-chip*` and `.set-dot` no longer have an emitter. Every `--spectrum-*` reference is gone rather than renamed — those names resolve only inside `<sp-theme>`, and this document is mounted in the Inspector's tab body, outside it, so each would silently have taken its hard-coded px fallback. The one deliberate change is the provenance chip: it is a `button` wherever it acts, drawn at the same 6px, because a 6px circle that clears a property was reachable by mouse alone.

& [part=\"empty\"].$description: The one empty-state pattern (`panels/empty-state.ts`), drawn here because a document cannot render a lit helper. Its rules are what is kept (§11): one sentence saying what the region is FOR, then the action that fills it.

& [part=\"rows\"][data-layout=\"grid\"].$description: The Size section only. Two equal columns that may both shrink to nothing, so a long value scrolls inside its own control instead of pushing the pane wider.

& [part=\"rows\"] > [part=\"row\"].$description: Scoped to the panel's OWN rows rather than to every `part="row"` beneath it, and that is load-bearing now that a colour row draws a `jx-color-field`. The kit is light DOM and one cascade, so `[part="row"]` as a bare descendant also matches the field's internal row — and at equal specificity with the kit's own `& > [part="row"]` the winner is whichever sheet was interned later, which is not a thing a stylesheet may depend on. The same reasoning moved `[part="chip"]` under `[part="chip-slot"]`, where `background: none` would otherwise have erased a swatch's colour, and `[part="control"]` under its row, where `> *` would have stretched a swatch's chip.

& [part=\"color-field\"] > [part=\"row\".$description: The field is `inline-flex` around a row sized to its own contents, which is right where it stands in a sentence and wrong where it IS the width of a dock. Two declarations, not a restatement of the kit's layout: the field still lays itself out.

& [part=\"chip-slot\"] > [part=\"chip\"].$description: One vocabulary, five states (§6.2). `default` draws nothing at all — absence IS the ghost — which is why there is no rule for it: the document never makes the node. `set` is the 6px accent disc `.set-dot` has always been; the two that carry information wear their donor's name in a bordered pill, and `mixed` is neutral on purpose because it says nothing about WHERE a value came from, only that the selection disagrees.

& [part=\"dot\"].$description: A collapsed heading has room for a tally, not for three labelled chips, so the two states that normally carry text collapse to coloured discs beside the accent one. That tally is what retired the tab's Active filter toggle: the toggle existed only because a closed section could not say whether anything inside it was set.

& [part=\"source\"].$description: The Value Source chip (§6.3): quiet while the value is a literal, accent-tinted the moment it is produced from something else. A CSS declaration has exactly two rungs — `JxStyle` admits no `$ref` — so the picker it opens is two rows, and that is derived from the schema rather than written here.

& [part=\"group\"].$description: The composite the kit cannot yet draw as one element: a field the reader may type anything into, beside a button that offers the values worth offering. `jx-combobox` is the element that replaces it (ui.md §5.3, Pending); until it lands, the field and the menu are two controls that abut.

children.$description: The Target Line's own host. It is EMPTY on purpose and stays empty: `surfaces/target-line.ts` mounts a second document into it, announced through `onNodeCreated` rather than found by selector (studio-ui-guidelines.md §9.4), so the line survives every repaint of the tab around it.

The inert half of the tally goes in the heading slot and the one control in the actions slot, which is the element's own division: a click on the actions row cancels the summary's toggle, and a click on an inert mark slotted there would cancel it for nothing.

group.$description: The dual-mode control: a number beside its unit, or a value beside the values worth offering. One shape for both because they are one gesture — type what you mean, or take one from the list — and the list is the kit MENU rather than a second popup of this document's own (§12.5).

color.$description: The colour row, and the whole of it: `ui.md` §5.6 landed, so the swatch, the value, the saturation square, the hue track and the project's own palette are ONE element rather than an announced `[part="control-host"]` a lit island filled. The listener is on the WRAPPER and not on the field, and that is the field's own contract rather than a preference. `jx-color-field` stops its five inner controls' native events at its root and re-says the platform's two names FROM the host, so an ancestor hears exactly one `input` and one `change` per gesture with `e.target` being the field — while a listener on the field itself hears BOTH, including the raw `change` of a text box holding a half-typed word the field has just refused. Bound there, `not a colour` would have been committed as a colour.

true.$description: The palette's `change` is caught HERE, on the group, because it never gets out: the field routes it as its `palette` channel, stops it, and then declines it — a swatch that stands for `var(--color-accent)` is not a string the field can parse as a colour, which is exactly why the reference survives the click. A row that let the field answer instead would have committed the literal behind the token and quietly opted one declaration out of the palette for ever.
